home.title: IoT Monitoring System
home.subtitle: Real-time monitoring with PiCarX (Quectel RM520N-GL 5G), ESP32 (Wi-Fi / LoRa) and DHT22
home.description: Environmental telemetry: PiCarX favors 5G via RM520N-GL with Wi-Fi fallback; ESP32 may use Wi-Fi and LoRa depending on firmware and hardware.

qr.title: Quick access to the system
qr.subtitle: Scan the QR code with your phone to open this IoT monitoring app.
qr.copyFailed: Could not copy. Copy the address manually.

featureDescriptions.wireless: PiCarX: Quectel RM520N-GL as the primary path (5G), Wi-Fi as fallback. ESP32: Wi-Fi and LoRa as deployed.
featureDescriptions.accurate: DHT22 sensor with high accuracy and reliability

banner.title: Advanced IoT technology
banner.subtitle: ESP32 (Wi-Fi and LoRa), PiCarX with Quectel RM520N-GL (5G preferred, Wi-Fi fallback) and DHT22.

documentation.pageSubtitle: UML views for engineering teams and stakeholders: context, runtime containers, API components, repository roles, deployment, and data flow.
documentation.intro: These diagrams clarify responsibilities and boundaries between the edge (publisher and sensor), the web API, storage (SQLite on the server), and this UI. The dashboard only uses HTTP and never talks to the database directly.
documentation.syncNote: Feel free to explore the diagrams and the platform documentation. If you have any questions, please contact the development team at k_jonasaugusto@ufg.br.

context.title: 1. System context
context.description: External actors (operators, PiCarX with RM520N-GL 5G / Wi-Fi, ESP32 with Wi-Fi and/or LoRa) and the IoT monitoring system as a black box.

containers.title: 2. Runtime containers
containers.description: Edge publisher, Flask app, SQLite file, and the React SPA — logical boundaries and HTTP/JSON interaction.

backendComponents.title: 3. Backend components (Flask)
backendComponents.description: Ingest routes, query routes, maintenance, optional legacy HTML UI, and the sqlite3 layer over the database file.

repositoryRoles.title: 4. Repository roles
repositoryRoles.description: How product code (code/), automation scripts (scripts/), and docs relate — the IoT runtime is not the same as deploy/CI scripts.

deployment.title: 5. Deployment
deployment.description: Examples: Docker Compose for dev, the Raspberry Pi agent, and optional cloud hosting (same HTTP contract).

sequence.title: 6. Sequence — data flow
sequence.description: Periodic ingestion (POST /api/ingest) and dashboard reads (GET /api/latest/…, polling).

project.title: About the Project
project.description: IoT monitoring system developed for demonstration of remote sensing technologies.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.communication: 5G preferred (RM520N-GL) with Wi-Fi fallback on PiCarX; Wi-Fi and LoRa on ESP32

info.title: Two implemented setups
info.description: The same backend accepts reads from ESP32 (Wi-Fi and/or LoRa, depending on your firmware) and from PiCarX with the Quectel RM520N-GL 5G modem—traffic prefers 5G, Wi-Fi is the fallback. Both use the DHT22 sensor.

esp32.description: ESP32 with DHT22; Wi-Fi and/or LoRa connectivity.
esp32.detail3: Connectivity: Wi-Fi and LoRa (depending on firmware and hardware)
esp32.detail4: HTTP ingest to the Flask API

picarx.description: PiCarX with DHT22 and Quectel RM520N-GL (5G preferred; Wi-Fi as alternative).
picarx.detail3: Traffic prefers 5G; Wi-Fi fallback when applicable
picarx.detail5: Same Flask API and server-side SQLite

piCarxDashboard.waitingAlertIntro: The PiCarX has not sent readings yet. Check:
piCarxDashboard.waitingBullet1: Quectel RM520N-GL has mobile data and a route to the internet
piCarxDashboard.waitingBullet2: Wi-Fi is available on the Pi as an alternative to 5G (fallback), if configured
piCarxDashboard.waitingBullet4: API URL (PUBLISH_URL) points to the correct server
